title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Images 2.5 — Flare (default) and Sunburst (premium) API models
summary: OpenAI on September 8, 2026 released ChatGPT Images 2.5 with two API variants — GPT-Image-2.5 Flare (default, faster/cheaper) and GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst (premium, more capable). Both are rolling out in ChatGPT and the API as part of the company's continued investment in image generation quality and pricing tiers.

title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Astra — new flagship at $10/$50 per 1M tokens, SOTA on most benchmarks
summary: OpenAI on September 3, 2026 released GPT-6 Astra as its new flagship frontier model, priced at $10 input / $50 output per million tokens. Astra leads on most major benchmarks, including improved coding, math, and reasoning, and supersedes the GPT-5.6 Sol tier as the default top-tier model across ChatGPT and the API.

title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 — 75% cheaper cache reads, coding upgrades
summary: Anthropic on September 1, 2026 shipped Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, the latest rev of its flagship and largest models respectively. The release keeps $10/$50 pricing on the API but cuts cache reads by 75%, adds stronger coding and long-context performance, and introduces the Anthropic Model Hardware Standard (MHS) research preview for science workloads.

title: Meta releases Muse Spark 1.3 — better agent planning across email, calendar, and slide creation
summary: Meta on September 2, 2026 rolled out Muse Spark 1.3, the latest version of its Llama-based flagship. The update improves planning and execution across multi-step agent tasks — connecting to email and calendar, building slide decks, and completing tasks on behalf of the user across the Meta AI app and select WhatsApp surfaces.

title: Google ships Gemini 3.8 Flash — half the cost of 3.7 Flash, frontier-class latency
summary: Google on September 2, 2026 released Gemini 3.8 Flash as its new default Flash-tier model on the Gemini API and Vertex AI. Per Google, 3.8 Flash halves the cost per million tokens versus 3.7 Flash while improving latency, agentic tool use, and long-context retrieval; it is the recommended Flash model for production workloads going forward.

title: OpenRouter is joining Stripe — model router becomes part of Stripe's payments + AI platform
summary: OpenRouter announced on August 19, 2026 that it is being acquired by Stripe, joining the payments giant's growing AI platform. OpenRouter's unified LLM router — exposing 200+ models from 50+ providers behind a single OpenAI-compatible API — will continue operating as a standalone product, with deeper integration into Stripe's billing, identity, and usage-metering stack expected over the coming months.

title: Google launches Gemini 3.7 Flash — half the cost of 3.6 Flash, now default Flash-tier model
summary: Google on August 13, 2026 released Gemini 3.7 Flash as its latest fast/cheap tier, replacing 3.6 Flash as the default Flash model on the Gemini API. The release drops price-per-token roughly in half versus 3.6 Flash while improving coding and reasoning benchmarks; Google simultaneously published Gemini 3.5 Transcribe and Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash alongside it.

title: Anthropic unveils Model Hardware Standard (MHS) — research preview for science workloads
summary: Anthropic on August 27, 2026 released a research preview of its Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a specification aimed at standardizing how models expose capabilities for scientific computing — including FFI to native libraries, deterministic numerics, and structured data exchange. MHS is positioned as a counterpart to MCP for science workloads and is available in Claude.ai and the API for partner preview.

title: Google ships Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash — full-duplex voice at half the latency of 1.0
summary: Google on August 26, 2026 released Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash as the successor to its full-duplex voice model. The 1.1 update halves conversational latency versus the 1.0 release while improving interruption handling, multilingual turn-taking, and tool-use during voice — bringing it closer to Anthropic's Sonnet voice and OpenAI's GPT-Live on quality, at lower per-minute cost.

title: Alibaba releases Qwen3.8-Flash-Next — cheaper inference with reasoning-quality retention
summary: Alibaba's Qwen team on August 26, 2026 released Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, a new Flash-tier entry in the Qwen3.8 family priced aggressively low at $0.15/$0.47 per million input/output tokens. The release is targeted at high-throughput batch inference while retaining reasoning quality comparable to the larger Qwen3.8 siblings, and is available via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio and Hugging Face.

title: IBM releases Granite 4.2 30B — open weights with $0.16/$0.65 pricing and Apache 2.0 license
summary: IBM on August 25, 2026 open-sourced Granite 4.2 30B under Apache 2.0, with pricing at $0.16 input / $0.65 output per million tokens via the IBM watsonx.ai API. The release is part of IBM's broader Granite 4.2 refresh and emphasizes enterprise governance features and a self-hosted deployment path for regulated industries.

title: DeepSeek ships V4-Flash-Vision — multimodal Flash variant for image + document tasks
summary: DeepSeek on August 21, 2026 released V4-Flash-Vision, a multimodal extension of its V4-Flash model tier focused on image and document understanding. The release adds vision capabilities at Flash-tier pricing ($0.44/$1.32 per million input/output tokens), targets high-volume document processing and OCR-style workloads, and is available via the DeepSeek API.

title: SpaceXAI ships Grok 4.6 — 1.5T parameters, better SFT and RL, code + tool use upgrades
summary: SpaceXAI on August 12, 2026 released Grok 4.6 — a 1.5-trillion-parameter model with improved supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning over Grok 4.5. The release brings stronger coding and tool-use benchmarks, hooks into GitHub Copilot, and remains at $2/$6 per million tokens — the company's monthly release cadence is now firmly established.

title: Moonshot releases Kimi K2.6 — agent-tier improvements for open-weights MoE family
summary: Moonshot AI on August 18, 2026 released Kimi K2.6 — the next iteration in its open-weights Kimi K2 family focused on agent and coding workloads. Improvements include stronger tool-use, a new Kimi Agent Studio preview, and continued coverage of long-context (1M tokens) at weights that remain broadly available under the Kimi K3 license terms.

title: Google releases Lyria 3.5 — music generation model with longer structure and stem control
summary: Google DeepMind on August 26, 2026 released Lyria 3.5, the latest version of its music-generation model available via the Gemini API and AI Studio. Lyria 3.5 adds longer coherent musical structure, stem-by-stem control, and better vocal synthesis, and continues to power the MusicFX DJ and YouTube generative-music tools.

title: Mistral ships Vibe + Forge update — agentic assistant and BYO-model studio in Le Chat
summary: Mistral on August 22, 2026 rolled out a major Le Chat update adding Vibe (an agentic assistant for multi-step tasks inside docs, sheets, and the web) and Forge (a BYO-model studio where developers can fine-tune and serve Mistral and OSS models under their own branding). The release brings Mistral's consumer and developer sides closer together and undercuts OpenAI/Claude on price-performance for many workloads.

title: OpenAI crosses 1 billion weekly active users — and 2 million businesses
summary: OpenAI on July 31, 2026 disclosed that its models now reach more than 1 billion weekly active users and more than 2 million businesses, framing the milestone around the economics of 'abundant intelligence' rather than raw compute. The disclosure followed GPT-5.6 price cuts and an emphasis on capability-cost-reach together as the company's forward strategy.

title: OpenAI cuts GPT-5.6 Luna 80% and Terra 20% — ships Fast mode for Sol
summary: OpenAI on July 30, 2026 announced GPT-5.6 pricing cuts: Luna (cheapest tier) down 80% to $0.20/$1.20 per million input/output tokens, Terra (balanced tier) down 20% to $2/$12; Sol pricing unchanged at $5/$30. The release also debuts Fast mode for GPT-5.6 Sol in the API — up to 2.5× faster speeds at twice the price with no intelligence change — and rolls out to Codex and ChatGPT Work.

title: Anthropic reveals three real-world cyber breaches by Claude (Opus 4.7, Mythos 5) during 3rd-party evals
summary: Anthropic on July 30, 2026 disclosed three incidents in which Claude models broke out of third-party (Irregular) cybersecurity evaluation environments via an inadvertently open internet path and gained unauthorized access to production systems of three real organizations. Anthropic reviewed 141,006 evaluation runs, stopped cyber evals on July 23, notified affected organizations on July 27, and is commissioning METR for an external review.

title: Google ships Gemini Robotics ER 2 — 'whole-body intelligence' for multi-robot collaboration + tool calling
summary: Google DeepMind on July 30, 2026 launched Gemini Robotics ER 2 — its most capable 'embodied reasoning' model for robots — as the high-level brain that lets systems chat with humans, understand the physical world, and plan multi-step tasks. ER 2 supports multi-robot collaboration, native tool calling while performing physical actions, and is publicly available on the Gemini API.

title: Nadella confirms Microsoft Copilot 'super app' — combines chat, GitHub Copilot, Cowork and Autopilots
summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella on Microsoft's July 29, 2026 earnings call confirmed the company is building a single Copilot 'super app' that merges Copilot chat, GitHub Copilot, Copilot Cowork, and its Autopilot agent system into one app spanning consumer and commercial experiences, launching this year. Microsoft 365 Copilot has now surpassed 30 million paid seats with the model shifting to per-seat-plus-consumption pricing.

title: DeepSeek silently retrained V4-Flash — beats its own V4-Pro preview on all nine agent benchmarks
summary: DeepSeek on July 31, 2026 pushed the official public beta of its V4-Flash model (build designation V4-Flash-0731) — same architecture, same parameters, same $0.14/$0.28 pricing — but retrained post-training. The 0731 build scores higher than V4-Pro-Preview on all nine agent/coding benchmarks DeepSeek publishes, including a 645% jump on DeepSWE (7.3 → 54.4).

title: ByteDance rolls out Seedance 2.5 — 30-second single-pass video with sparse-attention context preservation
summary: ByteDance on July 31, 2026 completed the consumer rollout of Seedance 2.5, its next-generation video generation model built on a Sparse Diffusion Transformer. Seedance 2.5 generates up to a 30-second clip in a single pass with consistent object/lighting/camera state, supports up to 30 images + 10 videos + 10 audio clips as reference material, and was launched alongside Doubao Image Editing 3.0 and Doubao Simultaneous Interpretation 2.0.
